P1.evidence: Frame delivered and agreed cleanly: 'Just want to understand what's going on with your fitness right now. What's working, what's not? What are you looking to achieve? And if we can help with that, we can go into all the details about what we've got going on, if that sounds good' — answered 'Sounds good.' Open question followed immediately: 'this is all like, how can we potentially help? What's going on?' P1a N/A — no setter suffix, and the call was handed over from another closer at short notice with no notes referenced.

P2.evidence: The injury work was excellent and the most thorough in the batch: 'what's been the timeline here?' established the full arc from a four-ligament rupture at 19 through ignoring the retirement advice to bone-on-bone arthritis now, and 'have you tried any type of mobility work for that?' plus 'Did it help?' established that Knees Over Toes failed. Work and schedule asked directly and produced the sedentary consulting picture. Training history properly established across three questions. Diet asked and answered honestly. But height and weight were never asked or mentioned at any point on a call where the prospect said 'I need to lose a lot of weight' — the only weight figure anywhere is a 15-20 kg loss in 2022. Age came out only as a by-product of the injury timeline. No health-conditions question, no sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: The phase where the buying decision is supposed to be made did not run. The prospect defined his own goal as 'consistency' in his opening answer and the rep accepted that as the goal for the rest of the call without going a single layer deeper. No aesthetics-and-function question, no strength-mobility-energy question, no 'something you want to do but can't'. The why-now probe was the one attempt — 'After three or four years of not really being consistent, what changed for you?' — answered 'Not much, just time', and it was not pushed. Two young children were mentioned three separate times and never became a stake; when the prospect finally said 'I just want to be able to play with my kids whenever I want to', it was at 00:31:49, after the price. The reflect-back at 00:11:03 was a competent list of obstacles ('the injuries... work... kids... something you enjoy... not having the discipline or the accountability') and got 'Yep. Indeed. Indeed.' — but it reflected mechanics, never meaning.

P4.evidence: Fully run and the strongest phase on the call. 'You said you have tried other programs?' and 'When was the last time you took an actual program?' covered the history; 'Was it the fact that they didn't keep you accountable during the program or is it after the program?' produced the precise failure mode — 'they send you either PDF or they give you a link to an app and then they sort of disconnect from you'; 'what exactly is keeping you from being consistent now?' produced the root cause in the prospect's own words — 'mostly just having no accountability. If I'm the one that's holding myself accountable, that's probably not going to happen.' P4f partial only because the rep delivered it as a summary statement rather than a question: 'it's not like a lack of knowledge, but just getting the push to get back to the right habits.'

P5.evidence: Absent entirely. A 35-year-old with degenerative bone-on-bone arthritis that worsens under excess load, two young children, three to four years of drift and a body he described as being on 'an uphill ballooning stage' — and no version of what the next two years cost him was ever put to him. There was no 'are you willing to settle for that', no 'why not', no line in the sand. This omission is why the commitment failure that followed had nothing to push against.

P6.evidence: The defining failure of the call. P6a was attempted as a needs-gap check rather than a belief check — 'Anything that you feel like you would need that doesn't have in the program? Or I guess, how do you feel about it?' — and got a non-answer, 'No, I haven't seen anything yet. So I don't know.' P6b was never asked. And P6c was inverted: the prospect volunteered the exact opposite of a clear yes — 'I would love to tell you I'm 100% committed, but reality is I've been there before and it hasn't worked out. So I'm also not going to lie to you' — and the script's instruction at that moment is to return to Phase 5. Instead the rep answered with 'it's pretty hard for it not to work' and presented the price ninety seconds later. Given a documented pattern of abandoning programmes, including one six weeks earlier, this is the single highest-risk moment in the batch for a refund or a churned client.

P11.evidence: Step 2 was clean — Trevor's onboarding call booked live for Tuesday 1:15pm Eastern with the time-zone gap worked out, plus email and mobile captured and a WhatsApp fallback arranged. Step 1 was not completed: the link was sent and opened but no payment was taken, and the prospect flagged a two-to-three-day cross-border transfer with no card taken as a backstop, leaving the deal contingent on an off-call action with only 'just shoot me a message whenever it goes through' as the follow-up mechanism. Step 3 is a miss — the agreement was described as arriving after payment processes, so nothing was confirmed or signed on the call. Step 4 was described as a future email sequence rather than actioned, though the rep did offer 'in the meantime, we can get you into the trainings'.

objection_plays.detail: Doubt was raised explicitly and about himself: 'I would love to tell you I'm 100% committed, but reality is I've been there before and it hasn't worked out.' None of the play ran. No 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', no pleasure-versus-pain question, no BRIDGE, no PLANE, no BURNED BEFORE — which is remarkable, since BURNED BEFORE is written for exactly this prospect, a man who has been let down by four or five previous programmes. The rep instead answered a question that had not been asked, defending the programme's efficacy when the prospect had already conceded the programme works.

A terms objection with no scripted play. 'With any situation like this, you have rights and responsibilities, so I have no clue what I'm entitled to, nor do I know what my responsibilities are.' The rep answered with process — app, form review, check-ins — and never once addressed entitlements, obligations, cancellation, refund conditions or what happens at the end of the term. The prospect then agreed to pay $6,000 without knowing any of it. The playbook has no move for a prospect who asks about terms rather than price, and this is the second call in the batch where that gap appeared.

Clinical-fit gap again, and this time the prospect did not even raise it — the rep did, glancingly: 'given the fact that you had, you know, the knee, the issues there, first thing we're going to do is get you on Trevor's mobility routine, making sure that you're not injuring yourself.' That is the improvised partial-value reframe the playbook already documents as a known gap. Nothing in the script prompts a clearance question for a bone-on-bone joint, and none was asked.
No stall — he asked what the next step was and took it.
Married with children but the decision was never made contingent on anyone.
Zero price resistance. The $6,000 was met with 'All right. That's fine.'
No timing objection; he wanted to start immediately and already owns the kettlebells.

notes: Best P4 in the batch and no P3, no P5 and an inverted P6 — the rep diagnosed the problem precisely and then never built a reason to act, which did not matter because the prospect had decided before the call. That is the risk: this closed on the prospect's own momentum, not on the process, and the one signal the process exists to catch was ignored. He said he could not honestly claim commitment, and the correct move at that moment is to go back to Phase 5, not to the price. Two children were in the room the whole call and were never made the reason. Separately, no money was taken and a $6,000 deal now rests on an unmonitored international transfer.
